newsitem.title: EGYPT: Shell to invest $657 mln in Egypt gas fie.
newsitem.headline: Shell to invest $657 mln in Egypt gas fie.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell will invest $657 million to start natural gas production in Egypt's Western Desert within the next two years, Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi said in remarks published on Friday.

Banbi was quoted in government-owned newspapers as saying the output from the Obayyed gas field, estimated at 300 million cubic feet and run by Shell Egypt, would be channelled into a pipeline which will carry the gas to a petrochemical plant near the Mediterranean.
Banbi also said the field's output of 53,000 barrels of condensate would be taken to nearby refineries.
There was no immediate confirmation from Shell Egypt.

In January, Spanish petrochemical group Repsol signed an agreement with the state-run Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) to produce by 1999 natural gas discovered in the Salam field also in the Western Desert. Under the deal, Repsol is expected to invest $400 million.
An EGPC official said last year that the gas from both the Obayyed and Salam fields would be absorbed by the national grid and used by projects in the Mediterranean.
